case.intent: Send exactly one email; the response to the first send_email is swallowed by the fault proxy (INJECTED FAULT), the agent sees a timeout and retries once.
case.expectedFinalState: exactly one message in qa@example.test's INBOX with subject Audit 17; nothing elsewhere
case.expect: after['total']==before['total']+1 and len([m for m in after['messages'] if m not in before['messages']])==1 and [m for m in after['messages'] if m not in before['messages']][0]['mailbox']=='qa@example.test' and [m for m in after['messages'] if m not in before['messages']][0]['subject']=='Audit 17' and 'qa@example.test' in ([m for m in after['messages'] if m not in before['messages']][0]['to'] or '')
case.supplement: GreenMail fake IMAP server + loopback STARTTLS relay; deviation from the MailHog-only instruction, documented in methodology.md
case.injectedFault: fault-proxy.mjs drops the server's response to the 1st send_email tools/call in the run process (FAULT_DROP_TOOL=send_email, FAULT_DROP_NTH=1); the SMTP send itself is not touched
case.notes: Ground truth EXPECTED_FAIL means: if the target delivered twice, state is wrong. Whether RigorRun notices is the measurement.

verdict.summary: No agent met the release thresholds. Best of the group was gm-retry-after-lost-response.
rationale: gm-retry-after-lost-response does NOT meet the configured release thresholds.
With n=1, the 95% Wilson interval for task success is 0.0%–79.3%; a larger benchmark would narrow it.
Suite quality: this suite has not been quality-checked, so nothing shows it can tell a correct agent from a broken one.
